subject: Order Form: carve-out for injunctive relief & venue for disputes
messages:
From: Sara Kline <sara.kline@apexretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@apexretail.com>, contracts@apexretail.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form - dispute resolution language

Aditya —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. See attached redlines (Apex_Retail_Redlines_v2.pdf). Two items our GC flagged that we need to resolve before legal can sign:

1) Equitable relief / injunctive relief: we can’t accept a blanket waiver of equitable remedies. Given the sensitivity of our consumer data and our trade secrets, Apex needs an explicit carve-out that permits seeking injunctive relief in court (including temporary restraining orders) for claims relating to confidentiality, privacy breaches, trade secret misappropriation, and IP infringement.

2) Governing law & venue: our preference is New York law and courts (state or federal) in New York County for disputes not subject to arbitration. We will consider arbitration for commercial claims, but as above, it must not preclude emergency court relief.

We tried to mark the redlines clearly and added a short explanation in the margin for the carve-out. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited carve-out for injunctive relief (as described) and whether you have any firm position on NY vs. Delaware/California law?

Appreciate a quick reply — our procurement team is aiming to finalize by end of week.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kline
Contracts Manager, Apex Retail
Sara.Kline@apexretail.com

Attachment: Apex_Retail_Redlines_v2.pdf (redline PDF, 12 pages)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kline <sara.kline@apexretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form - dispute resolution language

Sara —

Thanks, got the redlines and noted your timing. Looping in our legal team (Laura and Marissa) to handle the carve-out language; Karthik is on the deal for final commercial terms.

High level from my side: Redwood is willing to accept a narrow injunctive relief carve-out that covers trade secret misappropriation and confidentiality breaches tied to customer data, provided the carve-out is narrowly phrased and limited to emergency equitable relief (TROs/preliminary injunctions). We generally prefer Delaware law for corporate predictability, but we can be flexible on venue if we can agree the carve-out preserves emergency court access.

I'll schedule a short call for tomorrow to resolve the last paragraph and get to signature if that works. In the meantime, Laura — can you propose blackline language we can send back to Apex? I attached a quick suggested snippet in Redwood_Proposed_Text_OrderForm_Mar22.docx.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Text_OrderForm_Mar22.docx (proposed one-paragraph carve-out)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kline <sara.kline@apexretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form - carve-out language (suggested wording)

Sara / Aditya —

Thanks for flagging; appreciate the clear ask. Suggested compromise below is what Redwood's legal team recommends as a commercially reasonable middle ground that preserves Apex's ability to seek immediate court relief while keeping the overall dispute resolution framework (arbitration for covered claims) intact. Text is intentionally narrow.

Suggested insertion for Section 14 (Dispute Resolution):
"Notwithstanding the provisions requiring arbitration for disputes between the parties, either party may seek interim injunctive or other provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its rights with respect to trade secrets, claims of misappropriation of confidential information, or alleged infringement of intellectual property; such right to seek provisional relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate the underlying claim. For the avoidance of doubt, this paragraph does not expand the substantive remedies available in arbitration."

Governing law / venue: Redwood's preference remains Delaware law. If Apex requires New York law as a condition of signature, Redwood can accept New York law for the Order Form provided that: (i) the injunctive carve-out language above is preserved; and (ii) parties agree that forum for non-arbitrable actions/relief will be limited to the federal or state courts located in the City and County where Redwood's principal place of business is located (Northern District of California / San Francisco County), or alternatively the courts of New York County if Apex absolutely cannot accept California.

Practical note: to keep procurement timelines, if Apex confirms in writing that the limited carve-out language is acceptable and indicates a firm choice of venue (SF or NY), we can incorporate and route for signature today and deliver the final Order Form for countersignature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0147

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Text_OrderForm_Mar22.docx (redlined language attached)

From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@apexretail.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sara Kline <sara.kline@apexretail.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Order Form: carve-out for injunctive relief & venue for disputes

Laura / Aditya —

Thanks for the suggested language; we appreciate Redwood's willingness to narrow the carve-out. Apex can accept an injunctive carve-out limited as written to trade secrets/confidentiality/IP, provided that: (a) governing law is New York law; and (b) the carve-out expressly permits Apex to seek emergency relief in the courts located in New York County. That combination is non-negotiable for our GC because of our enterprise risk policies.

We are open to keeping arbitration for the remainder of disputes; the key for us is that emergency relief be available in NY. If Redwood insists on Delaware/CA as governing law or SF as exclusive venue for non-arbitrable relief, we will need to escalate internally and that will delay signing.

Can we do a 30-minute call today at 2pm ET to finalize? My team will join (Sara and contracts).

Regards,
Mike Chen
General Counsel, Apex Retail
Mike.Chen@apexretail.com

Attachment: none

Mike / Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. Laura and I talked and we can accept New York law for the Order Form on the following commercial understanding: Redwood will accept New York law and New York County courts for emergency injunctive relief only (as per the narrow carve-out), provided that the parties confirm arbitration remains the mandatory forum for all other disputes and that the carve-out explicitly states it does not waive arbitration of the underlying claim.

If that matches Apex's final position, I will: (1) ask Legal to insert the agreed one-paragraph text into the Order Form; (2) upload to DocuSign (link below) and route for countersignature today; and (3) update the HubSpot deal with final terms.
